You can use all three setups together.

note_tweet.text:
This paper from Google explains why AI agents can inherit months of improvements and still perform worse.

Researchers evolved an agent’s setup on Claude Opus, then moved it to Gemini. 

It scored below Gemini’s basic starting setup in every domain tested.

The prompts, tools and checks transferred. The reasons behind them were lost.

That left the next optimizer repeating failed experiments and removing fixes it didn’t understand.

Google’s solution is Self-Improvement Memory (SIM), a running record of experiments that captures:

> Each edit and the reasoning behind it  
> Expected results, written down before testing  
> Actual results, including failures  
> The model and benchmark used

The optimizer reads that history every round and adds its next experiment.

On Opus-to-Gemini workspace tasks, SIM delivered about 3× more improvement from the same starting score. 

It also finished ahead in 9 of 10 independent coding runs.

The experiment history turned out to be part of what made the improvements useful.

note_tweet.text:
Terence Tao warns that the race to AGI is becoming toxic, and OpenAI’s massive paper dump wiped out junior research projects overnight.

Here’s what Tao said in the interview.

He argued that the push to prove more theorems, get more press coverage and try out the latest AI tools came at the expense of understanding the math.

AI is making its way through the pool of open questions, he said, while adding few new ones for researchers to work on.

Tao had looked at about 10 of the roughly 300 papers. The volume alone made it hard to assess what OpenAI had released.

Several papers were still difficult to make sense of. Many hadn’t been closely reviewed, and one or two had errors and were retracted.

Tao said nobody from OpenAI was helping mathematicians sort through the work. From his perspective, OpenAI considered its part finished.

That left researchers with hundreds of papers they hadn’t asked for. Tao expects some will be useful and some will be rubbish. It’s still unclear how much falls into each group.

Vector search, graph, and SQL in one open-source embeddings database for RAG 🔥

It’s called txtai. 

It combines sparse and dense vector indexes, graph connections and relational storage in one Python framework.

Search vectors with SQL and explore relationships in the same data. 

Use it for semantic search or as a knowledge base for LLM apps.

> Embed text, documents, audio, images and video  
> Build RAG with citations, GraphRAG and topic modeling  
> Run agents with AGENTS.md and SKILL.md support through smolagents

Its pipelines handle prompts, QA, transcription, translation and summaries. 

Workflows connect them into microservices or jobs using multiple models.

Run models locally with Hugging Face or llama.cpp, or access Claude, OpenAI and Bedrock through LiteLLM. 

Connect through web and MCP APIs, with clients for JS, Java, Rust and Go.

It supports micromodels through to LLMs and scales across containers.

Python 3.11+. Apache 2.0. 70+ example notebooks.

Researchers proved AI has deleted every reason universities exist.

Harvard University tested one part of that claim. In a controlled study, 194 undergraduates covered the same physics material in an active-learning classroom or at home with a custom AI tutor.

Students using AI made more than twice the learning gains, scored 30% higher on the assessment and finished in less time.

The tutor asked questions, gave hints and adapted when students got stuck. They still had to work through the physics themselves.

Universities have offered expert teaching and a place to learn together for roughly 1,000 years. If a laptop can teach some lessons this well, what makes that experience worth $60,000 a year?
